title: Peaks in Array
summary: An element in an array is a peak if it is greater than its adjacent elements.
statement: An element in an array is a peak if it is greater than its adjacent elements. Given an integer array nums and a 2D array queries, process queries to count peaks in specified subarrays or modify array elements. Return results for the first type of queries in order. Note that the first and last elements of any subarray cannot be peaks.
constraints: nums has at least three integers; queries are [1,left,right] counts or [2,index,value] updates.
A counted peak must lie strictly inside the requested inclusive range and exceed both neighbors in the current full array.
Return one integer for each type-one query in order.
hints: Only an updated index and its two neighbors can change peak status.
Store peak indicators in a Fenwick tree for range sums; remove/restore affected indicators around updates.
Count indices left+1 through right-1; on update recompute position-1..position+1.
The indicator sum equals the number of current peaks, and locality proves no other indicator changes after one value replacement.
editorial: The indicator sum equals the number of current peaks, and locality proves no other indicator changes after one value replacement.

tests.explanation: After changing index three to four, no interior value is strictly above both neighbors.
The initial middle value is a peak; after the update it is not, giving [1,0].
